A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a constraint-based modelling approach can be used to infer the optimal metabolic state of the cell, and that the inferred metabolic fluxes can be used as a basis for the prediction of the diurnal starch dynamics.

the model of starch metabolism is able to capture the dynamics of starch accumulation in O. taurus, and that the model is able to predict the diurnal dynamics of starch content in O. taura from the gene expression data.
the diurnal dynamics of the starch profile in O. tautri is predicted from microarray data by a constraint-based metabolic modelling approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the transcriptional profiles of starch-related genes do not accurately reflect the activity of the relevant enzymes.

the diurnal changes in starch levels can be predicted directly from the microarray data, and that the diurnal dynamics of starch metabolism are regulated by a few key transcription factors, which can be identified by the analysis of microarray data.
the transcriptional control of starch metabolism is not sufficient to explain the observed variability in enzyme activities.
